title: Quantum Finance Benchmark Extraction
description: Structured extraction of quantitative benchmark data from quantum finance papers.

paper_id.description: Unique identifier derived from the source filename.

validation_passed.description: True when validation_errors == 0. Downstream consumers should filter on this.

scope.description: Thesis scope. Must be 'gate_based'. Quantum annealing, adiabatic, and pure QUBO-on-annealer work is out of scope.

primary_silo.description: Primary problem domain silo from Phase 1 taxonomy (PD-01..PD-10).

has_quantitative_results.description: Whether the paper reports any quantitative experimental results.

summary.description: 1-3 sentence narrative summarizing the key quantitative finding and comparison to classical baselines.

family.description: Gate-based algorithm family. Quantum annealing and pure-QUBO-on-annealer are out of scope; use 'qaoa' or 'grover' for QUBO formulations solved on gate-based hardware.

num_layers.description: QAOA depth p, VQE layers, ansatz repetitions.

convergence_criteria.description: When does the algorithm stop? E.g. 'max 1000 iterations', 'gradient < 1e-6'.

hyperparameters.description: Key hyperparameters as key-value pairs. E.g. learning_rate, alpha (CVaR), penalty_weight.

problem_formulation.description: How the finance problem is mapped to a quantum problem.

encoding_method.description: How classical data is encoded into quantum states. E.g. 'amplitude_encoding', 'angle_encoding', 'basis_encoding', 'QUBO', 'block_encoding', 'qRAM'.

objective_function.description: Mathematical formulation of the objective. E.g. 'minimize x^T Sigma x - mu^T x', 'QUBO with penalty terms'.

constraints_handling.description: How constraints are handled. E.g. 'penalty terms', 'XY-mixer', 'feasibility filter', 'Grover oracle'.

num_binary_variables.description: Number of binary/qubit variables in the QUBO/Ising formulation when solved on gate-based hardware (QAOA, Grover-on-QUBO, amplitude-estimation). Annealer papers are out of scope.

problem_hamiltonian.description: Hamiltonian form if specified. E.g. 'Ising with ZZ and Z terms'.

dataset_specification.description: Detailed dataset info needed to replicate the experiment.

description.description: Free-text dataset description when structured fields are not available.

date_range.description: Date range of market data. E.g. '2015-01-01 to 2020-12-31'.

benchmark_name.description: Named benchmark. E.g. 'S&P 500 daily returns', 'MNIST', 'UCI Credit'.

preprocessing.description: Data preprocessing steps. E.g. 'log returns, 252 trading days, z-score normalisation'.

train_test_split.description: How data was split. E.g. '80/20 train/test', '5-fold CV'.

two_qubit_gate_count.description: Total two-qubit entangling gate count (CNOT + CZ + iSWAP + ECR + native 2q gates). Superset of cnot_count. Used by P4 as a circuit-depth proxy for resource estimation. Prefer the paper's reported total; fall back to cnot_count if only CNOTs are listed.

error_correction.description: Error correction parameters if fault-tolerant analysis is discussed. Null when not applicable (the norm for NISQ experiments).

type.description: Hardware platform. Quantum annealers (D-Wave, adiabatic) are out of scope for this thesis.

noise_description.description: Free-text noise description preserved from LLM output during cleanup.

single_qubit_error_rate.description: Single-qubit gate error rate. E.g. 0.001 for 0.1%. Search for 'single-qubit error', 'gate fidelity', '1-F_1q'.

two_qubit_error_rate.description: Two-qubit gate error rate. E.g. 0.005 for 0.5%. Search for 'two-qubit error', 'CNOT error', 'CX fidelity', '1-F_2q'.

readout_error_rate.description: Measurement/readout error rate. Search for 'readout error', 'measurement fidelity'.

t1_time_us.description: T1 relaxation time in microseconds if reported.

t2_time_us.description: T2 dephasing time in microseconds if reported.

implementation_details.description: Details needed to replicate or build upon this experiment.

code_url.description: URL to code repository if available.

transpilation_target.description: Backend the circuit was transpiled for. E.g. 'ibm_brisbane', 'H1-1'.

classical_solver.description: Classical solver used for comparison/hybrid loop. E.g. 'Gurobi 11.0', 'CPLEX 22.1', 'scipy.optimize'.

classical_preprocessing.description: Classical steps before quantum circuit. E.g. 'PCA dimensionality reduction', 'feature selection', 'covariance matrix computation'.

classical_postprocessing.description: Classical steps after quantum circuit. E.g. 'COBYLA optimization loop', 'majority voting', 'statistical aggregation'.

total_execution_time.description: End-to-end wall clock time including classical pre/post processing.

quantum_execution_time.description: Wall clock time for quantum portion only.

quantum_fraction_of_runtime.description: What fraction of total runtime is quantum? E.g. 0.1 means 10% quantum, 90% classical.

variance_across_runs.description: Std dev or variance across independent runs.

num_independent_runs.description: How many independent runs/seeds were averaged.

num_layers.description: Variational ansatz layers/repetitions or QAOA p. Mirror of algorithm.num_layers for implementation context.

ansatz_depth.description: Ansatz circuit depth per layer, distinct from total circuit_depth.

p_rounds.description: QAOA p parameter (number of alternating operator rounds) if applicable.

classical_mc_samples.description: Number of classical Monte Carlo samples used as baseline. Search for 'MC samples', 'paths', 'classical shots'.

parameter_selection.description: How variational/annealing parameters were chosen. E.g. 'grid search', 'optimized per size', 'fixed', 'random initialization'.

instance_selection.description: How problem instances were selected. E.g. 'random', 'worst-case', 'adversarial', 'hand-crafted', 'real market data'.

classical_hardware.description: Classical hardware used for comparison. E.g. 'Intel Xeon E5-2680 single core', 'NVIDIA A100', 'MacBook Pro M1'.

complexity_analysis.description: Computational complexity comparison for Hoefler et al. (2023) quantum advantage assessment.

quantum_complexity.description: Big-O complexity of the quantum algorithm. E.g. 'O(sqrt(N))', 'O(N^2 polylog(N))'.

classical_complexity.description: Big-O of best-known classical algorithm for same problem. E.g. 'O(N log N)', 'O(2^N)'.

speedup_order.description: Order of quantum speedup relative to classical. 'none' = paper reports no speedup found. 'none_proven' = no proven asymptotic speedup exists for this algorithm family (theoretical status from literature).

constant_factor_quantum.description: Prefactor/overhead per quantum operation. E.g. error correction overhead ~1000x.

constant_factor_classical.description: Prefactor for classical baseline. E.g. 'highly optimised, <1ns per operation'.

total_operations_quantum.description: Total operation count for the reported problem size. E.g. '1.2e9 T-gates', '3.4e12 total gates'.

total_operations_classical.description: Total classical operations for same problem size.

crossover_n.description: Problem size N* at which quantum overtakes classical after accounting for constant factors.

wall_clock_quantum.description: Reported or estimated quantum wall-clock time.

wall_clock_classical.description: Reported or estimated classical wall-clock time for same problem.

hoefler_viable.description: Does the speedup survive constant-factor overhead per Hoefler et al. analysis? null if insufficient data.

provenance.description: Tracks data origin for key fields. Values: 'paper_reported' (explicitly stated), 'paper_inferred' (deduced from context by extractor), 'figure_estimated' (read from figure), 'derived' (computed from theory by compute_derived_fields), 'bridged' (copied from another field by extraction_loader bridge).

notes.description: Free-text notes on inference decisions, e.g. 'hardware.type inferred as simulator_statevector because paper uses Qiskit with no QPU named'.

advantage_assessment.description: Assessment of quantum advantage for this experiment.

advantage_status.description: Current status of quantum advantage for this experiment.

crossover_size.description: Problem size at which quantum is expected to beat classical (if discussed). E.g. '100 assets', '10^6 paths', or a number.

resources_for_advantage.description: Estimated quantum resources needed for practical advantage. E.g. '10000 logical qubits', '1M physical qubits', 'error rate < 10^-4'.

data_loading_bottleneck.description: Whether the paper identifies data loading/encoding as a bottleneck to advantage.

feasibility_horizon.description: When this approach could become practically useful.

limiting_factors.description: Key barriers to advantage. E.g. 'qubit count', 'noise', 'circuit depth', 'data encoding overhead', 'classical competition'.

maturity_level.description: Experimental maturity: L0=theory only, L1=noiseless sim, L2=noisy sim, L3=QPU ≤20 qubits, L4=QPU meaningful scale, L5=production-relevant.
